project_clusters.summary: A large, interconnected Skyrim/Elder Scrolls mod-design ecosystem focused on lore, scholarship, immersion, systemic gameplay, dialogue, balance, and reusable frameworks.
design_patterns: Prefer modular frameworks that other addons can extend.
Favor lore-grounded mechanics and exhaustive source/tag coverage.
Use structured spreadsheets as design databases and research indexes.
Design cross-mod integrations rather than isolated one-off features.
Use canonical topic IDs, aliases, parent/child relationships, and machine-readable data where possible.

architecture_findings.knowledge_framework_role: Knowledge Framework is intended as a reusable hierarchical lore-topic and immersive-study platform, not merely a content mod. It hand-tags books and many items with topic keywords, tracks topic mastery, exposes Papyrus hooks for new study methods, and is designed for modular JSON-driven extension.
interoperability: KID/string-based tagging for named lore items and books
Aliases for differently named custom content
Topic IDs should converge when multiple addons define the same topic
Actors, books, items and world objects can share topic/language semantics
Addons are expected to build gameplay on top of the same knowledge state
gameplay_family: Scholars of Skyrim: book hunting, publishing/royalties, autographs, lectures, apprenticeships, recommendations and consequences for dangerous research.
Silvertongue: language mastery, untranslated texts, scholar translation, speech/combat checks and learning from runes/world objects.
Apocryphal Knowledge: forbidden-knowledge progression with sanity/corruption-style consequences and integrations.
Arcaneum/Scholarship: book categorization, study fatigue and Humanities/Sciences/Metaphysics subject organization.
Codex: study-time-based spell learning/research with mastery thresholds, risk checks, fatigue, archetype knowledge and integrations.
Daedrologist: systemic Daedra summoning/bargaining with persistent knowledge such as nymics, disposition, allegiance, offerings and binding state.
architecture_findings.agent_os_implication: Model this ecosystem as a project graph with Knowledge Framework as a shared platform/data dependency and addons as related projects. Retrieve the framework contract plus only the relevant addon context for a task.

user_confirmed_structure.knowledge_framework: Base framework and shared knowledge/study platform.
user_confirmed_structure.arcaneum: Earlier concept that evolved into Knowledge Framework; may remain specifically as the book-tagging project/layer, but exact boundary is unresolved and should be consolidated later.
user_confirmed_structure.imperial_library: Primarily concerned with tagging existing lore books and/or adding lore books from prior Elder Scrolls sources.
user_confirmed_structure.addon_strategy: Most related mods should be frameworks themselves or integratable addons that compose with the shared frameworks.
user_confirmed_structure.version_policy: When redundant versions conflict, newer material generally takes precedence, but older versions should be preserved as provenance and compared for inconsistencies, gaps, useful abandoned ideas, and consolidation opportunities.

project_clusters.summary: Original fiction/worldbuilding project with multiple drafts and lore documents. Recurring elements include the Gravekeeper/Gravetender, Gallowed Man, Dennis Deacon, Avalon/Avalon Institute, the Void/Fade, runic/alchemical magic, contracts, Wardens, Makers, and black-humor supernatural action.
style_and_worldbuilding_notes: Mixes dark fantasy/urban fantasy, cosmic or metaphysical horror, tactical supernatural action, and irreverent black humor.
Worldbuilding is system-heavy: magic has terminology, costs, institutions, tactical applications, and technical logic.
Drive includes dedicated lore docs and magic-system docs rather than only prose drafts, suggesting a preference for explicit world-bible support.

second_pass_findings.source_state: Dream Eater Drive material spans multiple years and contains explicit notes that some terminology/graphics/definitions are out of date. Treat it as versioned worldbuilding, not a single internally consistent canon.
metaphysics: The Fade is framed as narrative/imaginative potential or unreality shaped by human perception; Earth is objective reality; the Otherworld is a reality-like formation within/from the Fade created through human perception.
Names are conceptual/contextual identity rather than simple labels and are central to magical control, identity, memory, contracts and spiritual decay.
Magic/Fade practice is strongly tied to understanding, worldview and subjective conceptual models; Avalon organizes practitioners into Houses/perspectives.
guardian_cycle: Guardian power was splintered into nine Emblems associated with the original Blades; later Emblems developed quasi-sentient identities influenced by their original wielders.
Emblems can accept, reject, sabotage or change wielders, so they function as relationships/characters as well as power sources.
The Guardian cycle spans multiple generations, with Mourn, Gallowbird, Incubus, the Nine Eyes of Avalon and later Deadlight Brigade material linked across generations.
contracts_and_spirits: Contracts are persistent metaphysical connections exchanging power/Name/agenda between humans and nonhuman entities; power imbalance and relationship affect influence and possession risk.
Wardens commonly encounter Shackled Ones in the Void, but contracts are not intrinsically Warden-exclusive.
Dream Eaters/Dreamless material connects identity decay, Names, memory consumption, death and the Nameless/Broken Throne system.
avalon: Avalon refers both to an extradimensional city and an organization; the public Avalon Institute is a nonprofit-facing arm while the larger organization regulates/researches magic.
The Eight Houses, Council, sectors, Prague Agreement, Black/White Index and Sector Seven establish a bureaucratic institutional layer around the magic system.
Avalon's history includes the War of Glass, centralization under Incubus/John Avalon, conflict with the Inquisition, Guild and Makers, and the Guardian cycles.
continuity_risks: Terminology is visibly in flux: Fade/Otherworld/Elsewhere, Nameless Throne/Broken Throne, Dream Eater/Dreamless, House labels and some laws of magic need canonicalization.
Several documents repeat or partially contradict explanations of Names, contracts, Guardian history and metaphysical geography.
Some notes explicitly mark concepts as OOD/revisit/unfinished, so document modification date alone should not automatically promote every statement to canon.
second_pass_findings.recommended_future_consolidation: Build a Dream Eater canon registry with concepts, aliases, status (canon/provisional/deprecated/question), first/last source, contradictions, unresolved questions and dependency links. Then consolidate world bible documents by domain without deleting historical drafts.

authority_order: Current manuscript is the strongest authority when it explicitly establishes something
user_confirmed_canon_policy.future_module: A separate writing-buddy/lorekeeper module should use this canon registry and actively challenge the writing/worldbuilding rather than merely retrieve lore.

silence_user_confirmed.definition: The Silence is a cosmic force that causes non-Fade users to forget Fade users, effectively making them disappear from ordinary historical/social memory.
silence_user_confirmed.narrative_role: It preserves the setting's Masquerade-like concealment of the supernatural and is intended to be central to the series.
silence_user_confirmed.note: Older sparse Drive notes describing The Silence should not be treated as the complete current definition.

manuscript_and_guardian_pass.authority_observation: The current 'dream eater' manuscript (modified 2025) should govern explicit story facts, but it remains visibly WIP with placeholders/author notes; draft prose from 2023 is useful as provenance rather than automatic canon.
current_manuscript_elements: Opening material centers the Gravekeeper/Gravetender and Gallowed Man at the Broken Throne, followed by Lilith Deacon.
The Gravekeeper visits deaths/contract moments and handles a seed associated with the dead person's remembered identity/story.
Current notes explicitly connect Lilith's Broken Throne arrival to uncertainty around Deadlight, personhood and having a Name.
older_draft_elements: Older Chapter 1 material foregrounds Abigail Fletcher as a teenage psychic whose magic manifests through individualized Mindscapes, attention, suggestion and perception.
Dreameater draft v1 foregrounds Dennis Deacon and a militarized magical conflict involving the Hand/Makers, runic arrays, Alchemists, Wardens, Shackled Ones and Code White threats.
These drafts establish tone and possible retained character/system material but should not override the current manuscript without confirmation.

guardian_cycle_sheet.freshness: Modified 2026-05-21, making it one of the freshest structured Dream Eater lore sources found so far, but unresolved cells and explicit undecided outcomes remain provisional.
guardian_cycle_sheet.structure: Maps four Guardian generations, Names/powers, vaults, fates, Emblem disposition and successors.
notable_links: Door ↔ Theft ↔ Vault of Change; later associated with the Gallowed Man/identity-death history.
Gallowbird ↔ Shield ↔ Vault of Absence; later Raven.
Incubus/John Avalon appears in the second generation and survives with a returned Emblem.
Third-generation Dennis Deacon is mapped to Ellison Crane as successor.
Dusk Morrigan maps forward to Reese Morrigan.
Melissa Finnegan maps forward to Abigail Fletcher.
Malia's Emblem is usurped by Deadlight and maps to Lilith Deacon/DEADLIGHT Virus.
Eric Ashland maps forward to Lotus Morrigan.
guardian_cycle_sheet.status_rule: Treat rows containing ???, Maybe, Undecided, probably, blanks, or contradictory fate wording as Provisional/Unknown even though the sheet is recent.

lorekeeper_requirements_emerging: Canon authority cannot be determined by modification date alone: manuscript authority, explicit user confirmation, document role and uncertainty markers all matter.
Track character identity/name inheritance separately from Guardian Emblem succession; they overlap but are not the same relation.
Track concept evolution across prose, lore docs and structured sheets, and preserve abandoned variants for comparison.
questions_to_resolve_later: How exactly does the newer Silence mechanic interact with Names, ordinary memory, written/digital records and institutional Fade-user memory?

gravekeeper_gravetender.definition: Gravekeeper and Gravetender are titles for Ellison Crane, currently referring to the same being. The wording/title may change later.

sequence: Door was the original Guardian who summoned Mourn.
After the Black Guardian was shattered, Door assumed the Guardian's responsibility for watching over the Nameless in the graveyard.
A child was transformed by Denial into a conceptual suicide bomb and sent as a homing weapon against the Nameless Throne.
The impact broke both the child and Gallow; their remnants coalesced into a gestalt.
Ellison Crane and the Gallowed Man function as two halves/aspects of that gestalt when Ellison puts on the mask.
door_gallowed_man_ellison.naming_note: Door's name is provisional and may be changed later.
door_gallowed_man_ellison.continuity_note: Older documents that describe Door, the Gallowed Man, Ellison, or the destruction of the Nameless Throne differently should be compared against this user-confirmed sequence rather than automatically promoted.

legacy_material: A 2022 Dream Eater draft uses older terminology including Black Sun/Midnight Sun, Wanderhouse, Sidewinder, Maw, Mist and Seladres around Dennis Deacon's opening operation.
The 2023 Dreameater draft preserves much of the same Dennis operation but updates terminology toward Makers, Wardens, Shackled Ones, Fade/Void and the later institutional vocabulary.
A 2023 Abigail fragment reinforces the gambling opening, psychic resource limits, family connections and her irreverent/comedic characterization.

An older Invocation brainstorm proposed spell Degrees as increasing removal from human rationality, with normal upper bounds around degree 6-7 and Harland reaching 11; this is an Idea/legacy mechanic unless supported by newer material.
evolution_signals: Dennis's opening is a strong example of iterative replacement rather than independent lore: scene architecture and jokes persist while organizations, magic vocabulary and threat taxonomy change.

Sidewinder appears to have evolved toward Warden; Maw toward Shackled One; Black/Midnight Sun material appears replaced or recontextualized by the Makers conflict. These are candidate mappings, not canon equivalences.
The repeated preservation of Dennis, Dusk, Avalon, squad structure, runic/alchemical combat and Void traversal suggests those are durable story/system anchors even when terminology changes.
deep_version_comparison.lorekeeper_design_implication: The future Lorekeeper should support lineage links such as renamed_to, evolved_into, replaced_by, retained_from and uncertain_equivalent, not only contradiction flags. It should compare scene-level revisions so retained ideas can be distinguished from terminology churn.
challenge_notes: Because The Silence is now central, older scenes involving large magical institutions, public-facing Avalon operations and supernatural combat will eventually need a consistent explanation of who can remember/record these events and how cleanup works.

The Name/identity system, Silence-based forgetting, Dream Eater memory consumption and Guardian/Emblem identity inheritance all manipulate memory or identity through different mechanisms. Keeping their boundaries explicit will prevent them from becoming interchangeable plot devices.

Avalon's public nonprofit face plus hidden magical-government role creates a useful pressure point: the setting will eventually need rules for how mundane staff, patients, governments and records interact with an organization containing Fade users.

cross_project_preferences_inferred_from_: The user tends to build large structured reference libraries before or alongside implementation.
The user values exhaustive coverage and completeness, especially for lore catalogs, character/item lists, and classification systems.
The user frequently decomposes ideas into reusable frameworks plus optional addons.

The user likes mechanics that make previously passive information actionable: books become study systems, lore becomes gameplay tags, artifacts trigger dialogue, forms become machine-classifiable templates.
Spreadsheets are often used as canonical design/research tables even when implementation later moves into code.
Project naming often uses concise thematic names followed by a descriptive subtitle.
Compatibility and extensibility with other mods/tools are recurring design concerns.
The user often revisits older concepts and evolves them over months or years, so preserving provenance, prior versions, and resumable project state is valuable.

drive_files_detected_but_intentionally_n: files whose primary purpose appears to be storing passwords or authentication information

retrieval_guidance: For Skyrim/Elder Scrolls questions, retrieve only the relevant subproject cluster and its current GitHub/project state; do not inject the entire lore corpus.
For Dream Eater writing, retrieve the worldbuilding cluster plus the specific scene/character/lore docs relevant to the request.
For LEGO/minifigure tasks, distinguish collection tracking, third-party release monitoring, and custom production/design as separate intents.
For HR tasks, prefer sanitized engineering knowledge and local-only processing; do not pull raw personnel content into durable memory.
For finance tasks, use current connected financial data when available rather than stale Drive budget snapshots.

For redundant project documents, prefer newer/current material for active context while retaining older versions as provenance; proactively surface contradictions, gaps, duplicated concepts, and potentially valuable ideas that disappeared between versions.
